bug_semantics: JdbcAssertingPartyMetadataRepository.AssertingPartyMetadataRowMapper reads the verification_credentials and encryption_credentials BLOB columns from saml2_asserting_party_metadata and deserializes them with Spring's DefaultDeserializer, which is unfiltered Java native ObjectInputStream deserialization. An attacker who can INSERT/UPDATE those columns can store a gadget payload; the next findByEntityId() or iterator() call then executes it on the SP JVM (CWE-502). Advisory range is Spring Security 7.0.0–7.0.5 (class @since 7.0); OSS patch is 7.0.6.
flaw_origin: The insecure sink was first written when JdbcAssertingPartyMetadataRepository was added in 16fd24c0025f2c1d77eafd59ddd59a0a42730e81 (PR #17077 / gh-16012): AssertingPartyMetadataRowMapper constructed `new DefaultDeserializer()` and called deserializeFromByteArray on the credential BLOBs (and originally also signing_algorithms). Later #save and polish commits kept that DefaultDeserializer; they did not introduce it. The 7.0.6 fix replaced it with Saml2X509CredentialCollectionDeserializer, which installs an ObjectInputFilter allowlist.
